title: Test and prune a writer's rules
statement: Treat every rule or example added to a writer's instructions as a change to test, and prune and reconcile the rules as they grow.
example: A run that added constraints and warnings fell from 65% to 61%.
detail: In the AP generator's prompt runs, a run that added constraints and warning text fell from 65% to 61%, and its analysis blamed added rules that created conflicting signals and 'do not' lists the model couldn't all satisfy (`icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/docs/archive/ITERATION_ANALYSIS.md`; `icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/docs/archive/VERSION_ANALYSIS.md`). Adding 15 document examples to one course's source-based essay prompt brought 4 failures, where the version without examples had passed 98% (`icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/docs/IMPROVEMENT_PROPOSALS.md`).
against: Examples helped elsewhere: another course passed 100% with 31 examples (`icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/docs/IMPROVEMENT_PROPOSALS.md`), and concrete bad examples correlated strongly with passing (`icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/docs/archive/VERSION_ANALYSIS.md`). The runs compared changed several things at once, and a 4-point drop may be within run-to-run noise.

evidence.quote: > **More rules ≠ better output.** The LLM has limited attention. Every added constraint dilutes the importance of existing ones.
3. **Conflicting DO NOTs** - Model couldn't satisfy all constraints
APUSH DBQ had 4 failures after adding 15 document examples to prompts.
